# Facet padding refutes fixed-threshold marginal lifting

This note refutes the auxiliary assertion that **every** integer marginal
center of depth at least `2^{-n}` has, somewhere in its fiber, a point of
mixed-integer depth at least `gamma_d 2^{-n}`. It does not refute OC, which
allows the fiber to be selected using the entire geometry.

## Facet-padding lemma

Let `d>=1`, let `D` be a full-dimensional compact convex body in
`R^n x R^d`, and let its mixed-integer volume be `M_0>0`. Fix `p in Z^n`
and a full-dimensional compact convex `d`-body `K` of volume `W>0`.
Introduce a new integer coordinate `u` and put

    C=conv(({0} x D) union ({1} x {p} x K)).

Then `C` is a full-dimensional compact convex body. Indeed its first
generating set has affine dimension `n+d`, and any point of the second
generating set is outside that affine hull. Its only supported integer
layers are `u=0` and `u=1`: the former is exactly `D` and the latter is
exactly `{p} x K`. These identities follow from the extremality of zero
and one in the range of the affine coordinate `u`. Thus its total
mixed-integer volume is `M_0+W`.

Write `delta_D(y)` for normalized halfspace depth in the old mixed set,
and `delta_C(0,y)` for depth in the new one. For every old supported point,

    delta_C(0,y) = M_0/(M_0+W) delta_D(y).              (1)

For the lower bound, a closed ambient halfspace containing `(0,y)`
restricts on the old layer to a closed containing halfspace or the whole
old space. Its old-layer mass is therefore at least `M_0 delta_D(y)`.
Its new-layer mass is nonnegative. For the upper bound, any old halfspace
`G={w:a dot w>=b}` containing `y` extends to

    G_L={(u,w):a dot w-Lu>=b}.

Choose `L>max_{w in {p} x K}(a dot w-b)`, which is finite by compactness.
Then `G_L` agrees with `G` on the old layer and misses the new layer,
including its boundary. Taking the infimum over `G` proves (1). No
infimum needs to be attained. All normals of the extended old halfspaces
are nonzero because their old normals are nonzero.

The same proof applied to the finite measure on integer coordinates gives
exactly the same identity for marginal depth. Consequently, if an old
integer point has marginal depth `beta` and

    W=M_0(2^{n+1} beta-1)>0,

its new marginal depth is exactly `2^{-(n+1)}`. If every point in its old
fiber has depth below `gamma_d beta`, the padded fiber has every point
below `gamma_d 2^{-(n+1)}`. Arbitrary positive `W` is realizable by scaling
one coordinate of a simplex. This statement intentionally assumes
`d>=1`; the unrestricted choice of `W` need not hold for counting measure.

## Rational counterexample with n=2 and d=4

Let

    T={x in R^4:x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1},
    lambda_0(x)=1-sum_i x_i, lambda_i(x)=x_i (1<=i<=4),
    V=vol_4(T)=1/24,
    r=1/10, epsilon=r^4=1/10000, B=rT,
    D=conv(({-1}xB) union ({0}xT) union ({1}xB)).

The old three integer fibers have volumes `epsilon V,V,epsilon V`.
The middle fiber is exactly `T`, because all generators lie in `T` in the
continuous coordinates, and it contains the generating copy of `T`.
The endpoint fibers are exactly `B` by extremality of their integer
coordinate. `D` is full-dimensional: `T` supplies four independent
directions at index zero and either endpoint supplies the fifth.

Define the rational simplex and padded convex body

    K=diag(3+2 epsilon,1,1,1) T,
    C=conv(({0}xD) union ({1}x{0}xK)).

The integer coordinates are `(u,z)`. The projection is the triangle with
vertices `(0,-1),(0,1),(1,0)`, whose only integer points are

    (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1), (1,0).

The corresponding fibers are `B,T,B,K`. All are four-dimensional and
all have positive volume. The total mixed volume is

    M=(1+2 epsilon+3+2 epsilon)V=4(1+epsilon)V.

The old marginal depth of `z=0` is

    beta=(1+epsilon)/(1+2 epsilon),

since either closed real-line tail containing zero contains the middle
fiber and at least one endpoint fiber; each of the two tails beginning
at zero attains that mass. Formula (1) for marginals therefore yields

    depth_marginal(0,0)=(1+epsilon)V/M=1/4.           (2)

For this `n=2,d=4` set, put

    gamma_4=(4/5)^4=256/625,
    tau=gamma_4(1+epsilon)=160016/390625.

The desired unnormalized OC mass is `gamma_4 M/4=tau V`. We show that
every point of the selected fiber `{(0,0)}xT` fails that mass threshold.
For a selected `x in T`, consider the five closed containing halfspaces

    H_i(x)={(u,z,w):lambda_i(w)-4u>=lambda_i(x)},
    i=0,...,4.                                      (3)

The barycentric function `lambda_0` is affine, which still defines an
ordinary halfspace after its constant terms are moved to the right side.
Its normal, and each other displayed normal, is nonzero. On `K`, every
`lambda_i(w)<4`: `lambda_0<=1`, coordinates 2 through 4 are at most one,
and coordinate 1 is at most `3+2 epsilon<4`. Thus (3) misses the entire
new layer, since `lambda_i(x)>=0`. On the old middle fiber, its volume is

    vol_4{w in T:lambda_i(w)>=lambda_i(x)}
      =(1-lambda_i(x))^4 V.                         (4)

This is a simplex homothety with center at vertex `i` and scale
`1-lambda_i(x)`; formula (4) also holds at the endpoint scales zero and
one. Suppose all five cap masses were at least `tau V`. On the endpoint
fiber `B`, `lambda_i<=r` for `i=1,...,4`. If `lambda_i(x)>r`, those
endpoint contributions vanish, and (4) implies

    lambda_i(x)<=1-tau^(1/4), i=1,...,4.

If `lambda_i(x)<=r`, the same bound holds because
`tau<(1-r)^4`. The `i=0` cap captures at most both entire endpoint
fibers, of total volume `2 epsilon V`, and therefore

    lambda_0(x)<=1-(tau-2 epsilon)^(1/4).

These inequalities cannot sum to one. The exact rational witnesses are

    a=8000199/10000000, b=7999223/10000000,
    tau-a^4=2032792963819263760799/10^28>0,
    tau-2 epsilon-b^4=664183074753367294559/10^28>0,
    4a+b-4=19/10000000>0.

They give `4 tau^(1/4)+(tau-2 epsilon)^(1/4)>4`. Summing the five upper
bounds would consequently give

    1=sum_i lambda_i(x)
      <=5-4 tau^(1/4)-(tau-2 epsilon)^(1/4)<1,

a contradiction. One of the five explicit closed halfspaces through
every selected point therefore has mass strictly below `gamma_4 M/4`.
Their masses are continuous in `x` because the continuous normals are
nonzero and the fibers have four-dimensional volume, so the boundary
hyperplanes have zero relevant measure. Their minimum is continuous on
compact `T`, is everywhere strictly below the threshold, and hence has
maximum strictly below it. The actual depth is bounded above by that
minimum. Thus the **entire** selected fiber has maximum depth strictly
below `gamma_4/4`, despite (2).

The example refutes the proposed fixed-threshold marginal lifting
principle. It does not refute OC: the newly added fiber has volume
`(3+2 epsilon)V`, which exceeds three quarters minus a small amount of
the total, and its own centroid already gives a larger depth guarantee
than `gamma_4/4` by ordinary Grunbaum applied to that fiber alone.

All numerical claims are verified by
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_facet_padding_fixed_threshold.py` using rational arithmetic.
